This notebook goes through one decision: see what you may trade, download prices, build a portfolio, check it and submit it. Run it chunk by chunk; nothing is sent until the `submit()` chunk.

## Setup

Install once:

```{r}
install.packages(c("pak", "tidyfinance", "dplyr"))
pak::pak("advanced-empirical-finance/aefsim/r")
```

Your team's token goes into `~/.Renviron` as `AEF_TOKEN=aef_...` (open the file with `usethis::edit_r_environ()`), followed by a restart of R. Never paste it into a script or notebook you share.

```{r}
library(aefsim)
library(tidyfinance)
library(dplyr)
```

## What can we trade, and under which rules?

```{r}
universe <- get_universe()
as_of <- attr(universe, "as_of")   # the latest close
as_of
count(universe, eligible, sp500)
```

Only `eligible` stocks can be bought: CRSP-style common stocks on NYSE, NYSE American and Nasdaq that closed at $5 or more. A stock you hold that drops below $5 may be held or reduced, not increased.

```{r}
get_parameters()                     # costs, shorting, leverage, position cap, and when they change
attr(get_calendar(), "next_deadline") # the next deadline, 09:00 New York time
```

## Prices

The simulation does not serve prices. tidyfinance downloads them from Yahoo Finance, the same source the simulation fills at.

```{r}
candidates <- universe |> filter(eligible, sp500) |> pull(ticker)
prices <- download_data("Stock Prices", symbols = candidates, start_date = as_of - 365, end_date = as_of)
```

## A simple rule

As an example (not a recommendation): the 20 S&P 500 stocks with the lowest volatility over the past year, equal weight.

```{r}
volatility <- prices |>
  arrange(symbol, date) |>
  group_by(symbol) |>
  mutate(ret = adjusted_close / lag(adjusted_close) - 1) |>
  summarise(vol = sd(ret, na.rm = TRUE) * sqrt(252), days = n()) |>
  filter(days >= 200)

picks <- volatility |> slice_min(vol, n = 20)
weights <- setNames(rep(1 / nrow(picks), nrow(picks)), picks$symbol)
weights
```

Weights are fractions of your portfolio's value. Tickers you leave out get zero, so this replaces your whole portfolio; whatever does not add up to one stays in cash.

## Check, then submit

```{r}
check <- validate(weights, as_of = as_of)
check
```

`validate()` runs every check the simulation runs and stores nothing. When it says OK, submit before the deadline. The rationale is your decision log: write down what you expect and why.

```{r}
result <- submit(
  weights, as_of = as_of,
  rationale = "Low-volatility tilt: equal weight in the 20 least volatile S&P 500 stocks over the past year."
)
result
```

Changed your mind? Submit again (the last accepted submission before the deadline is filled), or `cancel(result$submission_id)`.

## The next morning

Fills happen at the US open of the fill date; results appear after the nightly update.

```{r}
get_submissions()
get_portfolio()
get_performance()$summary
get_leaderboard()
```
